Hi Sarah / Tom \b

Thanks again for the time today, really appreciate the clear context on Acme's requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap of call:
- Use case: PHI-enabled clinical notes processing and triage for post-visit workflows.
- Key compliance asks: BAA required, SOC2 Type II evidence, US-only data residency, audit log retention (7+ years), KMS/HSM for key management, and periodic third-party audits.
- Deployment modes discussed: Hosted API (with BAA & controls), Dedicated (reserved capacity / stronger isolation), Private VPC or on-prem (highest isolation / customer-controlled networking).

Our initial recommendation based on the call:
- Pilot: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) - gives predictable throughput and stronger tenant isolation while we validate PHI flows and run through your security checklist.
- Long-term: Private VPC if your security team requires customer-managed networking or air-gap options. Hosted API with a signed BAA can work for lower-scope PHI workloads but has different operational guarantees (shared control plane vs Dedicated/Private).

Requested items from Acme to advance procurement / security review:
1) Share the SOC2 Type II report scope (or allow us to send the SOC2 attestation).
2) Any completed security questionnaire or control matrix you have (we can pre-fill where helpful).
3) Confirmation of data residency (US-only) and any additional legal clauses for the BAA.
4) Target timeline for pilot (e.g., 2-4 week pilot window) and procurement milestones.

Next steps I propose:
- I will send a short packet with: SOC2 summary, a BAA draft, and a short one-pager comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for HIPAA workloads. (cc: Dylan / Neha for technical follow-up)
- Schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive with Dylan (infrastructure lead) next week to walk through encryption, audit logging, retention, and integration patterns.
- Procurement sync between Tom and our sales ops to discuss contract timeline and any redlines.

Can you confirm (a) the right procurement contact (is Tom the lead?) and (b) any deadlines we should hit for your review cycle?

Thanks - talk soon.

Hi Sarah / Tom - quick follow-up and I’ve attached the packet I mentioned: 1) SOC2 summary (redacted high-level attestation points) and 2) a BAA draft for your legal team to review. Both are stubs here to get the ball rolling - happy to provide a fuller SOC2 attestation under NDA if needed.

Short answers to your bullets:
- KMS/HSM: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via integrations with AWS KMS / Google Cloud KMS and can support HSM-backed key stores for Private deployments.
- Encryption: TLS for transit; AES-256 at rest. Keys can be customer-managed for Dedicated and Private deployments; Hosted can be configured with customer KMS in many cases (we’ll confirm specifics in the tech call).
- Audit logs & retention: We can surface detailed audit logs (request IDs, tokenization events, user access) and support retention policies - we’ll confirm 7-year export workflows with Dylan during the deep-dive.
- Access controls: SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning supported for enterprise accounts.

Recommendation restated:
- If you want the fastest path to pilot and your legal team is comfortable with a signed BAA + hosted controls, Hosted + BAA could work for an initial, scoped pilot.
- If you need stronger tenant isolation / dedicated compute or want to limit control-plane exposure, Redwood Dedicated is our recommended pilot environment.
- If Acme requires customer-managed networking or an on-prem deployment for certification reasons, we’ll move to Private VPC / on-prem (longer lead time).

Attachments (included):
- SOC2_Summary_Acme_v1.pdf (redacted summary)
- BAA_Draft_Acme.docx
